#define MALLOC_CAP_INVALID          (1<<31) ///< Memory can't be used / list end marker

/**
 * @brief callback called when an allocation operation fails, if registered
 * @param size in bytes of failed allocation
 * @param caps capabilities requested of failed allocation
 * @param function_name function which generated the failure
 */
typedef void (*esp_alloc_failed_hook_t) (size_t size, uint32_t caps, const char * function_name);

/**
 * @brief registers a callback function to be invoked if a memory allocation operation fails
 * @param callback caller defined callback to be invoked
 * @return ESP_OK if callback was registered.
 */
esp_err_t heap_caps_register_failed_alloc_callback(esp_alloc_failed_hook_t callback);

#define portENTER_CRITICAL(mux)                     vPortEnterCriticalCompliance(mux)

#define portTRY_ENTER_CRITICAL_ISR(mux, timeout)    xPortEnterCriticalTimeout(mux, timeout)

findings.conclusion: Synchronous in allocation caller context after *_base returns. Current LIGHT-poisoned region allocator releases its mux before returning failure. This does not mean caller holds no other lock or that callback runs only in task context; heap port explicitly supports ISR callers.

One global callback pointer; NULL rejected, no unregister/chaining built in. Initialize immutable boot/session/ELF identity and fixed internal record before registering once, before network/scan; preserve repeated-init result and data. Existing project registration search had no competing hook at review start.

No heap traversal, allocation/free, printf/logging, NVS, SDK owner queries, task APIs or function_name dereference in hook. Fixed scalar DRAM writes and IRAM code; query formats after taking a consistent snapshot outside hook.

portENTER_CRITICAL_ISR uses infinite -1 spinlock timeout; short lock body does not bound cross-core acquisition. Recommended portTRY_ENTER_CRITICAL_ISR(mux,0): actual SDK attempts one compare-and-set and returns on contention. Preserve IRQ state. Mark capture incomplete on miss without a retry loop. Count/first/last mean recorded events, not guaranteed all allocation failures if misses occurred.

Prefer allocators report once only if all alternatives fail, with final attempted caps. function_name is allocator API, not vendor request caller. Requested size excludes internal alignment/poisoning overhead; record raw value rather than infer total physical footprint. Direct base allocator calls and returned NO_MEM paths need not all invoke callback.

Read-only MEMFAIL should bind session/boot/fullELF to current since-register record, have known/registration/incomplete/saturated distinctions, and never clear on query. Callback must not obtain identity via another lock or late global restamp.
